Boy oh boy did I have a delectable treat on the night of 8/27 at North Star Dining hall! As a freshman at Cornell University, I get unlimited meal swipes, essentially making dining hall food free. However, you could not pay me enough to eat the meal I just consumed for a second time. I waited in the longest line for food I’ve seen at Cornell just to be served the most diabolical dish I’ve ever seen. Let me begin by describing the vegetable options. I was offered an entire bush of broccoli (unchopped to edible size and hardly steamed) and half-cooked baby carrots (that I declined). I added some mashed potatoes to my plate with high hopes (soon to be dashed). After my third bite of the potatoes, my mouth began rejecting it frantically. I felt a slight burning sensation in my mouth as if it was spicy, but forced myself to continue as every other food facility on campus was closed due to the UAW strike. After I built up the courage, I took my chicken drumstick in my hand. It instantly went limp in my hand (bone and all) and all hopes I had for the meal vanished. I took a bite and sure enough, it felt as though I had taken a bite of a rubber tire. At that point, I resigned myself to being hungry. The UAW strike must come to a fair agreement with Cornell university as soon as possible for the sake of all the students.

reviews.author: - Decision
reviews.text: i think the workers in red t shirt are all student workers and i believe his name is kevin or something that ends in ‘in’ and he wears glasses. i only caught a glimpse of the little name pin while we walked past each other from the bathroom yesterday but this disgusting guy does not wash his hands after using the bathroom. please do something about your workers hygiene. 🤮🤮🤮

reviews.author: Stephen Yang
reviews.text: The definition of a local eatery in Central NY, Carol's Coffee and Art Bar on 177 Front Street in Owego oozes charm and friendliness while serving up tasty handmade menu items. The  everything bagel was a breath of fresh air compared to factory made bagels especially in taste and texture.  The coffee and tea were also excellent as was the entire friendly service team. And of course you'll be inspired and maybe even "surprised" at the high level of art being exhibited mostly by Carol herself! Bravo! #supportlocal

reviews.author: Sharon Poarch
reviews.text: Carols coffee and Art bar, a quaint coffee shop in Owego New York with art for sale and more coffee flavors that I’ve ever seen in my life! we had homemade cranberry orange bagels with bacon, egg and cheddar cheese sandwich. It was amazing!

reviews.author: Lana A LaBonte
reviews.text:
Carol is delightful! She immediately greeted me what a smile & shared all her Gluten Free specialties.
My Dad had the Bacon quiche with coffee & I had the vegetable quiche with a hot apple spiced cider with a cinnamon stick. I hadn’t had a hot cider in years so this was such a treat!
I also got a peppermint mocha on the way out with a couple slices of coconut cake.
My sister recommended this place & especially the GF coconut cake.
I had a bite of the coconut cake & it brought me back to my childhood when this was one of my favorite desserts!
I highly recommend you stop in to see Carol & the wall of all her & her daughter’s art!
It’s a homey feel with lots of love!

reviews.author: Kurt Weber
reviews.text: Quaint restaurant good for brunch breakfast and lunch. Interesting artifacts showing the history of coal being that this is an old coal weighing station. Order at the counter and they bring the food out to you right away. Park is a little tough as a lot of small and can only hold about six cars but we were lucky this time and parked in the small lot. Super friendly staff and very good food.

reviews.author: Kaitlyn Fedele
reviews.text: We were pleasantly surprised by how upscale this cafe was - the food was delicious and the atmosphere was perfect! We got the Ranch Eggs meal, crepes, and a vanilla latte. Everything really hit the spot and I'd say the pricing makes sense for the quality you get there. We also sat outside, there were a lot of seating options to choose from. Will be back again!

reviews.author: The Suave Sultan
reviews.text: A super cute cafe in a converted coal office building. They really lean into that heritage and have a lot of cool decorations and furniture that hail back to that era. The coffee and food are both very delicious and the staff are very friendly!

reviews.author: Alessandro Pigati
reviews.text: Probably the worst coffee I had in my life... And expensive as well! Bakery part is not as bad, though

reviews.author: Derek Rowe
reviews.text: Mattin's Cafe is convenient but not cheap.  They have a decent selection of wraps and other refrigerated fast food.  Their chocolate muffins are addicting, and for this reason I would recommend staying away from them!  Their prepared foods can be pretty decent, but their calzones are from the freezer and cost almost as much as freshly made calzones from DP Dough.

reviews.author: VJ Sat
reviews.text: Had the pleasure of ordering from Jackie a few days ago. She went above and beyond in my order during a very stressful time. The food was great and the customer service was even greater. Will definitely come back again!

reviews.author: Uno Roro
reviews.text:
Coffee is excellent, service is great (especially Serena),  nice decor/atmosphere, but food was extremely disappointing and overpriced.

Brie stuffed French toast -- it was dry
Fries -- portion is small and they charge $3
Homemade ketchup -- tasted like tomato paste
Ham and egg breakfast -- barely any ham

To top it off they add a "service fee" to your bill without even telling you.

Honestly, just come here for the coffee and service.

reviews.author: Urmilla Banerjee
reviews.text: Really nice for coffee and scones! Lots of interesting flavors of scones - we got chocolate earl grey and chocolate ginger. Both were delicious. There’s normally a wait for the brunch, but you can order the coffee and scones from the counter without waiting.

reviews.author: Aydan Scott
reviews.text: Mark has been here all three times we've visited over the last few months, and has always taken great care of us. This is the only place we've found in Ithaca so far that makes cappuccinos the same way we had them in Italy on our honeymoon and is a staple of me and my wife's dining experience in the area. The food is stellar every time we come here and we're certain to return time and time again.

reviews.author: Aszuaria Jones
reviews.text:
Nice laid back spot if you’re looking for a chill vibe.
Have been a patron here for a few years and it’s
Always been a chill vibe the hookah is amazing ( ask for the Anubis ) and the drinks are just right. This is a great date night spot also the Zeus fries chef Kiss . See you there .

reviews.author: Devon Strom
reviews.text:
Was recently introduced to this place by my buddy and I cannot suggest the Butter chicken enough. While it is not exactly the cheapest option for food. The quantity and Quality of it makes it easily an amazing deal especially for anyone who preps meals for work.

While I haven't participated in much of the other services provided here. I whole heatedly can endorse their food.

reviews.author: S A
reviews.text: This place is really awesome! I've been to a couple of hookah spots in Indiana, and this is definitely one I recommend. I hope y'all have a great time there, just like I always do.

reviews.author: David Bickford
reviews.text: Went here to grab a cup while waiting to see Kathleen Madigan at State theater.  Also, a cat rescue nearby.  Love the little guys!  Coffee was great, too! Around the corner from state theatre.  A place to stop by, and enjoy a cup of delicious coffee or tea.

reviews.author: Christine G
reviews.text: Please visit this adorable Cafe and adopt a cat if you are dedicated to loving cats. We had a great time here and if my sister and I didn't already have 12 cats between the 2 of us, we would have taken hone 2 or 3 of these lovey babies.

reviews.author: caitlin spry
reviews.text: First time coming here and I was immediately greeted by Queen Marigold who led to me to the room full of kittens! She was a sweetheart, all of them were! Most of them were sleeping so I didn't disturb them but when I got some toys out to play with the adults, that's when some of the kittens started to wake up. The little tiger I love so much, I'd adopt him if I could! He just wanted me to keep petting him, he was just purring and softly meowing, and I played with him too but he then snagged the toy right off of the pole! Such a playful kitten he is, I'll have to make another visit! All of the cats were friendly, of course some did get a little hostile towards others but not really in a fighting way due to the catnip toys so be mindful that they are cats and will do what cats do. I did get one of the espressos as well before I left and it tastes amazing, only about $6, and it's $5 for 30 minutes to visit the cats so that's not really bad and the money goes towards the cats too! I highly recommend stopping in, especially if you're looking to adopt then take a visit here first because there's plenty of kittens looking for a home.

reviews.author: Anastasja Moynihan
reviews.text: Ithaca’s premier breakfast and lunch location! They have a rotating menu of specials Friday-Monday that feature fresh seasonal local produce. They procure everything they can locally and make most items in house. The owners and staff really care about the community and food they serve. Everyone is friendly, accommodating and professional. They have great sandwiches - the witchwich, the Shannon, the Kara - fresh salads - omelettes - like the glorious or the Kai. Definitely check it out whether you’re just visiting the area or a local who just hasn’t made it in yet. You won’t regret it!

reviews.author: Sue Gould
reviews.text: Everything was great. The Kai omelet with kimchi and chipotle aioli was one of the best omelets I’ve ever had.  We also really liked the French toast and the cafe latte.

reviews.author: James Shealy
reviews.text:
Update:

Tried it again - spent $20 on cold gumbo (no faults with the chef - his cooking is good, just the service). I do not recommend this place; its only redeeming quality is the nice atmosphere.
______________________________________________

I've been here a few times and truly wish I could offer a better review. The food and atmosphere make this place one of the best spots to grab brunch in Ithaca. They have an ever-changing and very unique menu and the in the vibe is great.

However, I can't recommend this place purely on account of the very disorganized service. The last time I went with a group they lied to me about being able to seat us as opposed to just telling me that it would not be possible to accommodate my party (and this was not a large group where it would have made sense to call ahead). I don't mind if a place is full and can't seat any more people for the day, but I would prefer a measure of honesty about this. My group and I eventually left without ordering anything. To be very clear, the service is exemplary if you are actually able to get seated.

I don't believe that anybody individually was trying to be malicious, but it seems like there were multiple factors at work that caused this and that they seriously need to get a little better organized.

reviews.author: Alexander B
reviews.text: I’ve never walked into a place and felt more at home than I did at this establishment.  What drew me in were the windows decked out in houseplants, soft lighting from the globe lights hanging amongst the ceiling, and of course the great sounding menu. The drinks were amazing and customer service could not have been better. I walked in and was immediately helped. The staff was personable, super friendly and always went out of their way to make sure I was good. If you’re looking for a lounge with great drinks, music, soft lighting and overall great vibes, you gotta check this place out. You won’t be disappointed!

reviews.author: Danielle K
reviews.text: We only had drinks but the drinks were great and all 3 bartenders on Saturday evening during apple fest were wonderful! Very pleasant and custom made a shot from a loose recipie we had, and they were so fun! The plants hanging all over made the environment sooo relaxing and chill, such a cute place. We appreciated the vibe, the banter and delicious drinks, cant wait to come back!

reviews.author: SJ
reviews.text: Used to come here a lot. I was here yesterday and enjoying my matcha latte - until I have felt something in my mouth as I take my last sip. There was this white-pinkish, hard bead thing in the drink, still no idea what that is but that thing broke between my teeth as I chewed. The lady on the counter said she has no idea and mumbled that she is sorry, and didn’t offer me any refund or redoing the drink (it was other male staff member who made my drink fyi). Didn’t ask me if I was okay at all or anything - it was a very awkward moment. Having an unidentifiable object in your drink is a food hazard? Think it will be my last visit.

reviews.author: Blair SZ
reviews.text:
I've been eating at Ooy's for a year now.
I often order the John on gluten free bread and I usually get a Match Madness smoothie. The gluten free bread has always been soft and never had gaping holes like everywhere else. They also haven't charged me for gluten free bread ever, which I wish was a dining standard but oh well.
The food is always spot on for me. The service is always good too! Everyone is soo nice when I come in. They also always recognize me even when I drastically change my appearance.

So here's so problems people have pointed out.
The wait, I personally always go during times that aren't very busy and I don't worry about time often. HOWEVER, many people place their orders on the phone ahead of time so they can do pick up and eat outside.
The newer staff probably feel worse about the wait than you do.

Improper sandwichs: whenever something is lacking, I always go up immediately to alert someone when I'm in a restaurant. I always phrase it like, "this was probably a mistake but the egg on my sandwich is smaller than I'm used to when I get it here" 10/10 times I'm offered a remake or a discount.

Prices: if I could eat at Ooy's everyday I would but I am broke most of the time. However, I understand that the cost is due to the rising cost of living. I would much rather my local barista and cook have a livable wage than anything else. So... if I ever win the lottery, there would be signs and one of them would be eating there constantly.

reviews.author: Taylor Young
reviews.text:
Was in town looking for a good lunch spot. Most of the options in the area were restaurants. Saw this deli and it stuck out right away. I pulled up Google Maps to check the reviews and it had a pretty low rating. Most of the bad reviews were about coffee and slow service, neither of which were important to me at the time because all I wanted was a good sandwich.  So I gave them a try.

BOY DID THEY DELIVER! They had some interesting sandwiches on the menu, but I played it safe and went with the Classic Club. When it came out it I saw how big the portions were. The bread was nice and crispy and the sandwich was overall delicious. If I ever make it back I would try some of the other more exotic sandwiches.
This place is wayyyy underrated!

In response to the bad reviews: I didn’t try the coffee, but as far as service goes everyone was very nice. Slowness wasn’t an issue either, then again I was the only customer at the time.

reviews.author: The Suave Sultan
reviews.text: The sandwiches here are super tasty. I had the Rueben and it was one of the best I’ve ever had. Absolutely loaded with meat the and sauerkraut was tangy but not overpowering. The staff were really friendly and the service was top notch. This place it totally worth checking out.

reviews.author: Sorenmy Valdez
reviews.text: Awesome shop great staff with interesting personality the coffee shop interior is smaller feels bigger on pictures but it worth checking out we got the Salted NYS Maple Latte on ice and a hot latte butterfly pea. we felt in love with the Salted Maple amazing drink!!

reviews.author: Ellie B.
reviews.text: Press makes consistently wonderful lattes. I typically order oat milk and the texture is lovely--like drinking a cloud. Best place in town for a latte, hot or iced. They also have a cute little study space and outdoor seating.

reviews.author: Andrea Erb
reviews.text: Ordered a mocha it tasted good however I was not notified when it was done. I finally went up to the counter after seeing people who came in after me get their drinks. Just to make sure I had the right drink I asked and the lady was like yeah as if I was dumb for asking. Wish I was notified as I was getting situated with my work and there were only 3 customers total.

reviews.author: Yunong Shi
reviews.text:
Beautiful and cozy space inside the Canopy Hotel, with friendly service and clear effort from the kitchen to deliver quality dishes. That said, the overall dining experience was mixed. Most of the food was just average—the flavors leaned too salty, and portion sizes were noticeably small. The coffee was inconsistent; one of the cappuccinos I had was unfortunately among the worst I’ve tasted. The pizza was fine, but nothing memorable. The serving time is quite long, most tables wait for 20-30mins to get their food.

On the positive side, the black bean burger and the pan-roasted shrimp stood out as well-executed and flavorful. There’s potential here, especially given the stylish setting, but it still feels like they’re working out some inconsistencies in both the kitchen and barista station.

reviews.author: Michael Apollo
reviews.text:
Consistently Excellent – A Highlight of Our Annual Stay

We’ve been staying at the Hilton Canopy in Ithaca annually, and The Strand Café has become a beloved part of each visit. After long drives and early mornings, it’s the warm, inviting atmosphere and reliably delicious meals that make this café a true haven for our family.

Breakfasts are especially outstanding. The cappuccinos are top-tier—smooth, rich, and perfectly crafted (we’re quite particular about our coffee!). The Roasted Tomato Omelette is a standout, and we appreciate the thoughtful variety of both meat and vegetarian options on the menu.

On this trip, we were especially grateful for Blythe, whose warmth, attention to detail, and genuine care elevated the experience even more. Her bright smile and attentive service didn’t go unnoticed—thank you, Blythe!

Looking forward to many more meals here.

reviews.author: Robbie
reviews.text: Really good vegetarian options. Excellent rigatoni. We enjoyed it. Even their cheapest wine is my best this week.

reviews.author: Chris Jose
reviews.text: Chicken cutlets sandwiches were great. The flatbreads are okay and would advise if you’re studying for an exam and want to eat something quick. Great place to get smoothies as well.

reviews.author: Ray Zhou
reviews.text: Great variety but overall, the food is not that great compared to terrace, trillium, etc

reviews.author: Ben Wells
reviews.text: I come here at least 3 times per week and it’s always delicious with great vibes. Flatbreads and deli station are my personal favorites; smoothies and Starbucks are also great. Probably my favorite spot on central.

reviews.author: Sommaya H
reviews.text: Gorgeous new cafe in a convenient spot on campus. It gets a bit busy around peak hours but theres so much seating and so much space + offers hot food and Starbucks drinks. I will definitely be back here every week when i’m on central!!

reviews.author: Taylor Lea Thomas
reviews.text:
🚨 Yummy Alert! 🚨
The crab and corn soup is soooooo tasty! Try it.
Layout of the food area is a bit odd which creates a bad logistical flow for people getting food and those exiting with their food. Also, the staff are seemingly unfriendly and I swear I thought the guy serving in the hot food section was going to drip sweat into the curry. The older lady next to him served the rice so sloppy. The dish looked ugly because of how it was served and presented and so I left it. But, the crab and corn soup is fantastic!

reviews.author: Yusong Jin
reviews.text: Gorgeous! Dandan noodles is awesome!

reviews.author: Farhana Yasmin
reviews.text: One of our most favorite dining rooms on campus. There’s a great variety of food every day, so it never feels boring. The halal and kosher stations are a big plus and not something found in other dining halls. The vibe is always lively, and the space is big enough that even when it’s crowded, we can still find a nice spot to sit and enjoy our meal.

reviews.author: Yunong Shi
reviews.text:
Hands down the best university dining hall I’ve ever experienced. Open to the public at $16 for adults and ~$7 for kids, it’s an absolute steal considering the quality and scale. The space is massive and beautifully designed, even equipped with a “Discovery Kitchen” for live courses and cooking demos.

The food stations are incredibly diverse: halal, West Side Grill, East Side Market, North End Pizza and Pasta, salad bar, dessert bar, fruit bar, yogurt bar, ice cream (from Cornell Dairy!), and more. Even in summer break, with some stations closed, the options were overwhelming in the best way.

Highlights:
•	The pizza was top notch – fresh from wood-fired ovens.
•	Blueberry and banana yogurt? Dreamy.
•	The grilled fish was surprisingly delicious.
•	Tater tots and salad bar were far above average – packed with thoughtful toppings like artichoke, chickpeas, beets, and tuna salad.
•	Desserts were solid; the brownie was rich, and we had fun making waffles ourselves.
•	The ice cream options, while not mind-blowing, are generous and fun to explore (and hey, it’s Cornell Dairy).

If I were a student here, I’d never want to eat off-campus. Absolute envy.

reviews.author: Teng Ren
reviews.text:
Best dinning hall in US universities. Totally blown away by the quality and variety of the foods. I had the best pizza in America so far. There are red pizza, white pizza, all kinds of toppings, and the crust is made perfect, all freshly from the real fire oven. Price is also very reasonable.
All foods are made to high quality restaurants standards.
